title: The database refuses to edit, add to or delete a published place snapshot and its parts; only published to superseded, a source's scheduling facts and a page named for the next run (nothing collected) move
steps: S1: On a database migrated by the package, edit, insert into and delete the profile, sources, media links and import row of a published snapshot, and change its state, place, scope and published_at.
S2: Carry a later run's tries onto the published snapshot, record an operator verdict on a social page, revoke a picture, supersede the snapshot.

S3: Tracy's chain (with 173, the copy of 0004) is adopted with carried: ['0004-place-snapshot-guard.sql']; undeclared, adoption is refused naming the guard; a database adopted at the baseline alone gets 0004 from the package.
expect: S1: every write is refused with 'place snapshot guard'.
S2: every write succeeds; superseded cannot go back to published or be deleted.
S3: verifyWoSchema reports no difference and the marker rows name the adopted files.
evidence: wo_place_snapshot and its four child tables had no trigger, unlike wo_place_media and wo_social_snapshot
fence: Triggers wo_place_snapshot_immutable and wo_place_snapshot_*_immutable; adoptWoSchema/verifyWoSchema compare a host's carried later files as applied

tests: a snapshot being prepared is the run's own
published content cannot be edited, added to, or deleted
a published snapshot may name a page for the next run, but never what was collected
after publication only the lifecycle and the sources' scheduling facts move
an import or backfill writes a published snapshot and its parts in one transaction
a snapshot that never published can be failed or set aside
Tracy's full chain reaches the target
a host that does not declare the guard it carries is refused adoption
a database adopted at the baseline alone gets the guard from the package
Tracy's copy of each package file it carries is the same SQL

history: 24/10/2026: merging #1687 (add a social page by hand) — a source row or ref that only names a page, with nothing collected, is allowed on a published snapshot; collected data stays immutable.
